title: ClaimScene — narrated demo walkthrough
description: Per-beat, audio-locked script. build_video.py synthesizes each narration line (ElevenLabs), locks the beat's visual duration to the measured audio, and renders a gentle Ken Burns move across the committed cards in demo/assets/ — real captured screenshots of the running app plus two title cards. check_video.py re-verifies the rendered mp4 against this file. Refreshed 2026-08-02 to match the current product: forensic-CGI illustration seeded from the deterministic schematic, burned-in disclosure, computed camera push, sealed authorship split, direct-manipulation review, and async submit+poll render.

beats.caption: Honest accident documentation. Illustrated, never faked.
beats.narration: After a crash, the first real job is documentation. Which cars, which damage, which road, and what actually happened. ClaimScene turns accident photos into a case a claims handler can trust. Honest, illustrated, and never faked.

beats.caption: A convincing AI guess is dangerous as evidence.
beats.narration: That matters now, because generative video made accident scenes easy to fake and hard to trust. A convincing AI reconstruction that is really just a guess is dangerous as evidence. Insurers and courts are already warning about synthetic media in claims.

beats.caption: Photos in. A closed vocabulary out, never coordinates.
beats.narration: Every case starts with photos, yours or a sample scenario like this one. A vision model reads them into a closed vocabulary only: vehicle kind, colour, approach, and a twelve position clock for damage and impact, never a free coordinate.

beats.caption: Drag to move. Drag the handle to rotate. Nothing sealed yet.
beats.narration: The proposed scene is yours to correct. Click a vehicle to select it, then drag it between the four approaches, or drag its handle around the twelve clock positions. Every edit snaps to the same closed vocabulary, and the schematic redraws live.

beats.caption: One click. The app submits a render job and polls.
beats.narration: Confirm, and rendering runs as a background job the app submits and polls, since a real illustration render can take minutes. First the deterministic schematic, then the disclosed AI clip, then the sealed manifest.

beats.caption: The schematic is the reconstruction. The clip is a labeled illustration.
beats.narration: Here both layers sit sealed side by side. The schematic on the left is deterministic, drawn by code. The clip on the right is seeded from that same schematic, so its layout is inherited, not requested. A camera push toward the point of impact is computed too, and the disclosure is burned into the pixels, not just asked for in a prompt.

beats.caption: The model supplies style. Everything provable is computed.
beats.narration: The sealed manifest states that split in plain language. The geometry, camera path, and disclosure caption are computed by this codebase, never invented by the model. The model's real contribution is visual style only. Treat the schematic as the reconstruction, and the clip as a stylised illustration of it, never the reverse.

beats.caption: Press Verify. Eighteen checks re-run from stored bytes.
beats.narration: Press Verify, and the SHA-256 seal recomputes right in your browser. Behind it sits a receipt of eighteen named checks, each re-run from the stored bytes on the server.

beats.caption: 100% weighted field accuracy, on the record.
beats.narration: And the accuracy is measured, not asserted. The primary model scores one hundred percent weighted field accuracy on a committed seven scenario evaluation set, with a dated scoreboard living in the repo.

beats.caption: Live on Cloud Run. Open source. Never faked.
beats.narration: ClaimScene is live on Cloud Run, built on Genblaze and Backblaze B2, and the whole project is open source. Honest accident documentation. Illustrated, and never faked.
